technique_note: 13r l.8-10 (after the verses): الاصل تقنعيني وليس يلحن فلا توهمه منهم فان حذف النون جائز على التقدير ('the underlying form is tuqni'inani; it is not a solecism, so do not suspect it of them: dropping the nun is permissible by implication') - a remark on the word تقنعني/تقنعي of this verse, which the cipher spells تقنعي; then l.9-10 وكتب للمخدوم المشار اليه اسبغ الله ظلاله من نظم الشريف ... introduces the next block (13r.11). Nothing introduces 13r.1 itself: the page opens with it.

plaintext.text: [ا]لاثام اين الحجى اين التقى تقنعني بقولهم هذا اوزير الشام
plaintext.folio_lines: 13r l.6 (الاثام, last word of the first verse; its alif is enciphered at the end of 46v l.13) and 13r l.7 (second verse). Read as written on the master: 'اين' twice (dot under the tooth), 'اوزير' (interrogative a-wazir). The text AS ENCIPHERED is: لاثام اين الحجى اين التقى تقنعي بقولهم هذا وزير الشام

fit_check: fits exactly: 44 signs = 44 letters of the text as enciphered (لاثام اين الحجى اين التقى تقنعي بقولهم هذا وزير الشام), 10 groups = 10 words with the group lengths 5,3,5,3,5,5,6,3,4,5 equal to the word lengths. Every repeated letter takes the same sign (ا = E 9 times, ل = triangle 4 times, ي = T 6 times, ن = H 3 times, ق = K 3 times, م = 8 3 times), and the key is the same as the one that reads 46v.11. Against the master's wording (46 letters) the cipher drops one nun of تقنعني and the interrogative alif of اوزير; the lam of الشام was first omitted and written above the line. The earlier test of 13r l.5-8 against the 12v blocks is superseded: 13r l.5-7 answers 46v.11 + 13r.1.
notes: The block is the second half of one cipher whose first half is 46v l.11-13 (قلت لنفسي حين مالت الى وزاره الشام وفعل + the alif of الاثام): the text is split inside the word ا|لاثام across the two blocks, and both use the same alphabet and key. In the present binding f. 13r follows f. 12v, not f. 46v, so either a leaf (or more) is displaced or the copyist split the cipher; worth a codicological check (13v->14r and 47v->48r read continuously, so it is not a simple swap of ff. 13 and 47). Consequence for 12v.8 and 12v.11: their low-certainty candidate plaintexts (13r l.5-8) are taken by this chain, so they are left without a plaintext. Water stain over rows 1-3 (right half) blots the two crown signs (C1 in row 1, C3 in row 3); their values come from the plaintext. Theme: the compiler's own verses on the vizierate of Syria (cf. 45v l.10-12, 46r-46v).

count_method: by eye on plain ~2x crops (output/ljs51/crops/wmiss/102_row*.png); every group is closed by a dotted-stem divider, including the last group of each row; the double triangle in row 1 counted as one sign (it stands for one letter, ك). segment.py not used for the count.
transcription_eye: R->L: r1 SH2 B6 | HM W B6 A3 | Ta Fh DD N8 | Q Z C | ; r2 L Z E | SHy Q W C N8 | SH2 L F E | ; r3 L F2 E | SHy Hd W C N8 | SHy L Z E | ; r4 Q2 W | Q Z A3 |  (SH2 = sin-teeth with loop, B6 = 6-shaped loop with ascender, HM = loop with stem and right stroke, W = waw-like loop, A3 = ayn with long base, Ta = ta-shape, Fh = small lam/dal hook, DD = double triangle on one base, N8 = small 8 (numeral eight), Q/Q2 = loop with stem up-left and tail down, Z = ayn-ra zigzag, C = small open loop, L = lam hook, E = loop with tail down-right, SHy = loop with rising stroke, F = 9-shape, F2 = 4-shape, Hd = ha with tooth)
style: cursive Arabic-letter-like signs (sin-ha, 6-loop, ayn shapes, 9 and 4 shapes, small eight, double triangle, lam hooks); dotted-stem dividers; black ink, no red. A different alphabet from 48r.8 (which ends at the foot of 48v)
technique_note: 49r l.4-5 right after the block: فلم تنحل الا بعد تعب كثير / لصعوبتها وفيها شيخ[?] على تلك اللغز[?] ومما ('it would not come apart except after much toil because of its difficulty ...'), then the two verses l.6-7; l.8-13: فلما نظرت حالي معه في الحل مع ظني انني فيه بارع ولي تصانيف فيه وما احللت هذه الا بعد جهد وانه حل البيتين المتقدمين مع انهما اصعب من هذه سريعا ... كما فعله ابن دنينير في مصنفه وغيره ('I solved this only with effort, while he solved the two preceding verses, harder than this, quickly ...; Ibn Dunaynir recorded easier pairs of verses in his book').

plaintext.text: هتفن ضحى على بان بسلع سواجع كم سلين شج يرجع / سفكن دمي وما يدرين شوقا ولا يدرين يوما در دمع
plaintext.folio_lines: 49r l.6-7 (two verses). The block enciphers only the last 12 words: شج يرجع / سفكن دمي وما يدرين شوقا ولا يدرين يوما در دمع (master: شجٍ with tanwin, دمعِ with kasra - not شجو / دمعي as in earlier records)

fit_check: fits exactly for the enciphered part: 42 signs = 42 letters and 12 groups = 12 words, group lengths 2,4,4,3,3,5,4,3,5,4,2,3 equal to the word lengths of شج يرجع سفكن دمي وما يدرين شوقا ولا يدرين يوما در دمع; no sign takes two letters (ر = W 4 times, ا = E 4 times, م = Z 3 times, ن = N8 3 times, و = L 3 times, ج = B6 twice, ع = A3 twice, ش = SH2 twice); ي has three signs (HM, C, SHy) and د three (Q, Q2, Hd) - homophones or variant forms. Rows 2 and 3 repeat (وما يدرين شوقا / ولا يدرين يوما). The first eight words of verse 1 (هتفن ضحى على بان بسلع سواجع كم سلين, 28 letters) have no cipher on 49r; the 70-letter, 20-word pair does not fit 42 signs. The earlier tie of these verses to 48r.8 is wrong (48r.8 is answered by 21r, see recheck file).
notes: The block begins mid-verse at the top of the page, and 48r.8 on the facing 48v breaks off mid-text (at ربها جملته of the 20r.8 saj'): both point to a leaf lost (or displaced) between ff. 48 and 49, which would have held the rest of 48r.8, its solution remark, the introduction of this piece and the cipher of هتفن ... سلين. The sentence 'not solved except after much toil' (49r l.4-5) refers to this block. 49r l.5 word after وفيها read شيخ[?] (perhaps شبه).
